syscalls.comment: Mount, namespace, module, key-management, tracing, io_uring, clock and NUMA control. Each is an escape primitive in its own right or the sibling of one that is: the mount-API family (fsopen/fsconfig/fsmount/fspick/move_mount/open_tree/mount_setattr) sits here rather than relying on CAP_SYS_ADMIN being absent, and pidfd_getfd/kcmp sit here because ptrace is already denied. crates/deepsand-core/tests/seccomp_profile.rs asserts this set, so dropping an entry fails a test rather than a review.
ENOSYS rather than EPERM: clone3 takes its flags in a struct the filter cannot read, so it is refused outright and glibc falls back to the argument-filterable clone(2) below.

Deny clone() when any CLONE_NEW* flag is set. One rule per bit, because several args in a single rule are ANDed and SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ can only test one bit at a time. CLONE_NEWUSER is the important one: it creates a namespace without needing any capability, and it is how the userns-dependent class is reached. The privilege-requiring bits are already refused by the empty capability set; listing them too means the closure does not depend on that second control surviving.

CLONE_NEWUSER (0x10000000) - the load-bearing one, since it needs no capability. For anyone editing these: with SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ the first value is the MASK and valueTwo is what the masked bits must equal. Setting only the first means (flags AND mask) == 0, which matches every call that does NOT set the bit - that inverted all eight of these rules and made them block fork itself, so every sandbox exited on start with: FATAL tini (1)] fork failed: Operation not permitted
AF_PACKET (17): raw frames. Denied because a registered family that is not IP has no business here, and this one gives direct access to the link layer.
AF_TIPC (30): cluster transport, historically reached through container boundaries.
AF_ALG (38): kernel crypto sockets, usable without any capability.

AF_VSOCK (40): this is F3. On a Hyper-V or VMware guest it reaches the host or the hypervisor directly, which is how round 1 of the escape assessment obtained a root shell in the Docker Desktop VM. The measured EAFNOSUPPORT on this family is only attributable to seccomp because the kernel was shown to have registered it (/proc/net/protocols, /sys/module/vsock, the VMBus device); on an unregistered family the kernel returns the same errno by itself.

socketcall is the 32-bit multiplexer for socket(2); it cannot be argument-filtered here, so it is refused whole. Only the families above are enumerated: seccomp cannot express "family not in a set", so an unregistered family is left to the kernel, which refuses it too. Enumerating is why a kernel that registers a new dangerous family needs a new rule - the durable answer is an allow-list default action, which is not what this profile does.
